turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Okay, let's get started. This is the weekly sync for the payments platform. Arjun, Meera, thanks for joining. We have three things today: the latency issue, the caching plan, and the release on the twenty-fourth.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Sure. So the p99 latency on the checkout API went up to four hundred and twenty milliseconds last week. Most of it is coming from repeated PostgreSQL queries for the merchant config.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: Yeah, I saw that in Grafana too. The p50 is fine, it's only the tail.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Okay. Arjun, you had a proposal for caching?

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Right. I want to put Redis in front of the merchant config table, with a five minute TTL. In staging, that brought the p99 down to one hundred and eighty milliseconds.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: Five minutes is fine for config data. I'm okay with that.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Great. Then let's go with Redis for the merchant config cache. That's decided.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: There was also the idea of moving the event pipeline to Kafka.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: I'd honestly like to do that, but not this quarter. We don't have the bandwidth.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Agreed. We are not migrating to Kafka this quarter. Let's revisit it in January.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Now, action items. Arjun, can you ship the Redis cache behind a feature flag by Thursday?

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Yes, I'll have it behind a flag by Thursday.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: And I'll write the rollback runbook for the cache.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Thanks. We also need to update the on-call rotation before the release.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Yeah, someone should do that.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: And maybe Rohan could look into the flaky integration tests, but I'll have to ask him first.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: One open question. Do we have budget for the extra GPU nodes for the fraud model? It's around two thousand five hundred dollars a month.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I don't know yet. I'll check with finance and get back to you by Monday.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: One more thing. The OAuth token refresh bug is not blocking the release, so I'd keep it in the backlog.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Fine, it stays in the backlog. Okay, the release is still on the twenty-fourth. Thanks, everyone.

decisions: Use Redis as a cache in front of the merchant config table (5-minute TTL)
Do not migrate the event pipeline to Kafka this quarter; revisit in January
Keep the OAuth token refresh bug in the backlog (not blocking the release)
not_agreed: Move the event pipeline to Kafka (deferred to January)

action_items.task: Ship the Redis cache behind a feature flag
Write the rollback runbook for the cache
Check GPU node budget with finance and get back to Meera

not_confirmed: Look into the flaky integration tests (Rohan was only suggested; Priya still has to ask him)
